title: Menger's theorem, edge version for graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $x$ and $y$ be two of its vertices. Then the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint $(x,y)$-paths in $G$ equals the minimum number of edges whose deletion destroys every $(x,y)$-path in $G$.
hypotheses_covered: two vertices x and y of G
replaced:
(Menger; edge version for graphs). \emph{Let \texttt{x} and \texttt{y} be two vertices
of a graph \texttt{G}. Then the maximum number of edge-disjoint \texttt{(x, y)}-paths in
\texttt{G} is equal to the minimum number of edges whose deletion destroys all
\texttt{(x, y)}-paths in \texttt{G}.}
